senses.definition: To put things into a bag or container so you can carry or store them.
senses.example: Please pack a towel in your swimming bag.

senses.definition: A group of animals, especially wolves or dogs, that live or act together.
senses.example: We heard a wolf call to the rest of its pack.

senses.definition: A bundle or set of things sold, stored, or carried together.
senses.example: We bought a pack of blank cards for the project.

senses.definition: A small piece of a network message together with information that helps move it.
senses.example: A longer message can travel in many packets.

senses.definition: A tool with a broad, flat end used to move a small boat through water.
senses.example: The paddle slipped out of my hand and floated beside the canoe.

senses.definition: To move through water by pushing it with a paddle or with your hands or feet.
senses.example: We paddled slowly toward the beach.

senses.definition: One side of a sheet of paper in a book or other written work.
senses.example: A tiny map on the last page showed all the places in the story.

senses.definition: One document you can open on a website.
senses.example: The page for our school play lists the show times.

senses.definition: A special public show, ceremony, or display, often with costumes.
senses.example: Our town's pageant showed scenes from its history.

senses.definition: A tower with one or more levels and specially shaped roofs, found in parts of Asia and often connected with Buddhism.
senses.example: The garden path led past a stone pagoda.

senses.definition: A bucket.
senses.example: We carried a pail of water to the sand castle.

senses.definition: A colored liquid or paste put on a surface and allowed to dry.
senses.example: We chose yellow paint for the wooden birdhouse.

senses.definition: To put paint on something or make a picture with paint.
senses.example: Layla painted a row of boats along the shore.

senses.definition: A person who makes pictures using paint.
senses.example: The painter captured the red sky with just three colors.

senses.definition: A person who puts paint on walls, furniture, or other surfaces as work.
senses.example: The painter finished the ceiling before starting the walls.

senses.definition: Two things, people, or animals that go together or are used together.
senses.example: I found a pair of clean socks.

senses.definition: To put two people or things together, or connect one to another.
senses.example: We will pair the new readers with partners.

senses.definition: Clothes usually worn for sleeping.
senses.example: I put on warm pajamas before I read in bed.

senses.definition: A friend you know well.
senses.example: I brought two snacks so I could share with my pal.

senses.definition: A large, grand house where a ruler or other important person lives or once lived.
senses.example: The palace had a hall large enough for hundreds of guests.

senses.definition: The roof of the mouth.
senses.example: When I make the “sh” sound, my tongue rises toward the palate.

senses.definition: Light in color or less bright than usual.
senses.example: We made a pale green by adding white paint.

senses.definition: Having less color in your face than usual.
senses.example: I looked pale when my stomach hurt.

senses.definition: A flat wooden or plastic platform used to move or stack goods.
senses.example: The heavy bags were piled on a pallet.

senses.definition: A small book or folded set of pages that gives information about one topic.
senses.example: A pamphlet showed a map of the museum.

senses.definition: A thin, flat cake made by cooking batter in a pan.
senses.example: I turned the pancake over when its top filled with bubbles.

senses.definition: An organ behind the stomach that makes helpers for digestion and sends messages such as insulin into the blood.
senses.example: The pancreas helps the small intestine break food down.

senses.definition: A name used for two different kinds of mammals from Asia. The giant panda is a black-and-white bear. The smaller red panda has reddish fur and is not a bear.
senses.example: A giant panda sat among the bamboo stems.

senses.definition: A single flat piece of glass held in a window or door.
senses.example: A leaf stuck to the wet window pane.

senses.definition: One of the areas in a comic, often a box containing a picture or words.
senses.example: The next panel showed what was inside the box.

senses.definition: A sudden sharp pain or a strong feeling that comes on quickly.
senses.example: I felt a pang of sadness when the fair ended.

senses.definition: A sudden strong feeling of fear that can make it hard to think clearly.
senses.example: I felt a moment of panic when I could not find my ticket.

senses.definition: To become suddenly so afraid that it is hard to think clearly.
senses.example: My cat panicked at the noise and hid under the couch.

senses.definition: A closet or small room where food and dishes can be stored.
senses.example: I found the oat cereal on a low shelf in the pantry.

senses.definition: A tropical fruit usually with yellow or orange flesh and many round black seeds.
senses.example: We scraped the black seeds out of the papaya.

senses.definition: A thin material made of fibers, often used for writing, printing, or wrapping.
senses.example: I folded a piece of paper into a hat.

senses.definition: A written assignment or report on a subject.
senses.example: We wrote a short paper on birds that live in the park.

senses.definition: A book with a flexible cover made from heavy paper or card.
senses.example: The novel was printed as a lightweight paperback.

senses.definition: A group of people, vehicles, or animals moving along a route for others to watch.
senses.example: We watched the drum band lead the parade.

senses.definition: To move as part of a display or show yourself off.
senses.example: We paraded around the room in costumes we had made.

senses.definition: A group of sentences about a main idea, usually set apart from the next group.
senses.example: I started a new paragraph when the scene moved to the park.

senses.definition: Side by side and going in the same direction without getting closer or farther apart.
senses.example: We used a ruler to draw two parallel lines.

senses.definition: An electric circuit that gives current more than one path to follow.
senses.example: One lamp in a parallel circuit can be off while another keeps shining.

senses.definition: A four-sided flat shape with two pairs of parallel sides. In each pair the sides run in the same direction and stay the same distance apart.
senses.example: One piece in the puzzle was a slanted parallelogram.

senses.definition: A package wrapped or boxed for delivery.
senses.example: The parcel had our name and street number on it.

senses.definition: One piece of land treated as a unit.
senses.example: The town bought a parcel of land beside the school.

senses.definition: A writing material made from carefully prepared animal skin.
senses.example: The museum kept the old parchment protected from strong light.

senses.definition: To forgive someone for a mistake or an offense.
senses.example: Please pardon me for leaving the door open.

senses.definition: A polite word used to excuse yourself or ask someone to repeat what they said.
senses.example: “Pardon?” I asked when the last word was too quiet to hear.

senses.definition: A person who has or is raising a child.
senses.example: A parent helped us build the cardboard theater.

senses.definition: An animal or plant that produces young or seeds.
senses.example: One parent bird brought food while the other stayed near the nest.

senses.definition: Curved marks that enclose part of a sentence or calculation, like these marks around an example (2 + 3).
senses.example: The parentheses tell us to do that addition first.

senses.definition: A public outdoor area where people can rest, play, or enjoy nature.
senses.example: We walked to the park after breakfast.

senses.definition: To stop a vehicle and leave it somewhere for a time.
senses.example: Please park the bikes beside the gate.

senses.definition: A warm coat that usually has a hood.
senses.example: I wore a thick parka on the snowy hike.

senses.definition: A bird with a curved beak and strong grasping feet, often with bright colors.
senses.example: The green parrot perched on the top of the branch.

senses.definition: To repeat something that another person said without thinking about it or understanding fully.
senses.example: I parroted the words but could not explain what they meant.

senses.definition: A plant with fragrant green leaves used to flavor or decorate food.
senses.example: I added a little chopped parsley to the soup.

senses.definition: A piece or portion of something larger.
senses.example: I built the left part of the cardboard castle.

senses.definition: The job someone does in a shared activity or the character someone plays in a story.
senses.example: I got the part of the gatekeeper in our play.

senses.definition: To split or move away from each other.
senses.example: The curtains parted as the music began.

senses.definition: A very small piece of a substance, such as a speck of dust.
senses.example: Tiny particles of flour floated above the bowl when I stirred too fast.

senses.definition: In science, a tiny object such as an atom or one of the bits that make up atoms.
senses.example: A proton is a particle found in the center of an atom.

senses.definition: Someone who works with you, plays on your side, or shares an activity or part of life with you.
senses.example: My lab partner read the timer while I added the water.

senses.definition: To work together with someone or another group.
senses.example: Our class partnered with the library for the reading challenge.

senses.definition: To move by or beyond someone or something.
senses.example: Three buses passed our house while we waited.

senses.definition: To give something to someone or send a ball to a teammate.
senses.example: Please pass the cup to the person next to you.

senses.definition: To do well enough to succeed on a test or meet a requirement.
senses.example: Everyone in our class passed the bike safety test.

senses.definition: A ticket, card, or permission to enter a place or use a service.
senses.example: I showed my pass at the rink entrance.

senses.definition: A person traveling in a vehicle without being its driver or a crew member working on it.
senses.example: Each passenger had a seat near a window.

senses.definition: A secret you enter to help prove that you are allowed to use something.
senses.example: We chose a password so other people could not sign in to our account.

senses.definition: A tool that stores and helps you use your passwords safely.
senses.example: With a trusted grown-up, we used a password manager to keep track of different passwords.

senses.definition: Belonging to a time before now.
senses.example: We looked at pictures from past field trips.

senses.definition: Time that has already happened.
senses.example: The old bridge tells us something about the town’s past.

senses.definition: Beyond, after, or by a certain place or time.
senses.example: We walked past the corner store on the way home.

senses.definition: A soft colored stick used for drawing.
senses.example: I drew the sunset with an orange pastel.

senses.definition: Light and soft in color.
senses.example: The shop window held dresses in pastel shades.

senses.definition: A small area different from what surrounds it, or a piece used to cover a damaged spot.
senses.example: A patch of snow remained in the shade.

senses.definition: To cover or repair a hole with an added piece.
senses.example: We patched the tear in the tent.

senses.definition: A strip of ground that people can walk or ride along.
senses.example: A narrow path led through the garden.

senses.definition: A route that something follows or a series of steps toward a result.
senses.example: We traced the path of the sock across the muddy floor.

senses.definition: Able to wait or keep trying without becoming angry or upset.
senses.example: We were patient while the librarian looked for our book.

senses.definition: A person receiving care or treatment from a health worker.
senses.example: The nurse called the next patient into the room.

senses.definition: An arrangement that repeats or changes in a way you can describe.
senses.example: The beads followed a red, blue, yellow pattern.

senses.definition: A short stop before something begins again.
senses.example: After a pause, the singer started the next verse.

senses.definition: To stop for a short time.
senses.example: Pause the video so I can see the map.

senses.definition: A hard surface laid on a road or path.
senses.example: A worm wriggled across the wet pavement.

senses.definition: The foot of some animals, especially one with soft pads and claws.
senses.example: The cat stretched one paw toward my shoe.

senses.definition: To scratch or push at something with a foot.
senses.example: The dog pawed at the back door until I let her in.

senses.definition: To listen, watch, or think carefully about something.
senses.example: Pay attention to which plants grow closest to the water.

senses.definition: Money given to pay for something, or the act of paying.
senses.example: Our first payment covered the supplies for the class.

senses.definition: A time or condition when people or countries are not fighting.
senses.example: The two groups made peace after years of fighting.

senses.definition: A quiet or calm feeling.
senses.example: There was a sense of peace in the garden at sunrise.

senses.definition: A male peafowl, known for spreading long patterned feathers during a display.
senses.example: The peacock opened its feathers like a big fan.

senses.definition: The top or pointed highest part of a mountain or other shape.
senses.example: We could see snow on the mountain peak.

senses.definition: The highest point reached in time, amount, or strength.
senses.example: The park has the most visitors at the peak of summer.

senses.definition: To rise to the highest point before falling or staying lower.
senses.example: Water use usually peaks on hot days.

senses.definition: An edible seed that grows in a pod underground on a low plant.
senses.example: I cracked the dry pod and found two peanuts inside.

senses.definition: A fruit that is usually narrow near the stem and rounder at the other end.
senses.example: The ripe pear was soft and sweet.

senses.definition: A smooth, often round object that can form inside an oyster or other shellfish.
senses.example: The jeweler showed us a necklace made of white pearls.

senses.definition: A kind of moss that grows in wet places and can help build up peat from its old parts.
senses.example: Bright green peat moss grew on top of the soaked peat.

senses.definition: A small stone, often worn smooth by water or wind.
senses.example: I put the round pebble back beside the stream.

senses.definition: A substance plants make that can help a fruit mixture become thick and soft.
senses.example: Pectin helped the jelly keep its shape on the spoon.

senses.definition: Unusual or surprising.
senses.example: A peculiar smell came from the shed after the rain.

senses.definition: Found with one person, group, or place in a special way.
senses.example: The birds made a call peculiar to that kind of heron.

senses.definition: A part that you push with your foot to make something work.
senses.example: Pushing the pedal made the bicycle move.

senses.definition: To move a bicycle or a similar machine by pushing with your feet.
senses.example: We pedaled slowly up the hill.

senses.definition: A stand or base that holds something up.
senses.example: A stone birdbath stood on a low pedestal.

senses.definition: A person walking rather than riding in a vehicle.
senses.example: A pedestrian waited for the crossing light to change.

senses.definition: To look quickly or secretly, often through a small opening.
senses.example: I peeked through the curtain to see if the show had begun.

senses.definition: One quick or secret look.
senses.example: Can I take a peek at your finished drawing?

senses.definition: To take off or come away from an outer layer.
senses.example: I peeled the orange over the compost bin.

senses.definition: The outer skin of some fruits and vegetables.
senses.example: A strip of orange peel curled on the cutting board.

senses.definition: Someone around the same age or at the same level as you.
senses.example: At chess club I got advice from one of my peers.

senses.definition: To look closely because something is hard to see.
senses.example: We peered into the dim shed for the missing ball.

senses.definition: A short piece of wood, metal, or plastic used to hold or hang things.
senses.example: My coat hung from a peg by the door.

senses.definition: To fasten or mark something with a short pin or stake.
senses.example: We pegged the edge of the blanket to the ground so it would not blow away.

senses.definition: A large water bird with a long bill and a stretchy pouch underneath it for catching fish.
senses.example: A pelican dipped its wide bill into the water.

senses.definition: A writing tool that uses ink.
senses.example: My pen left a blue line on the page.

senses.definition: A small space closed in by a fence, often used to keep animals.
senses.example: The goats stayed in their pen until feeding time.

senses.definition: A tool for writing or drawing with a thin stick of graphite or colored material, often inside wood.
senses.example: I sharpened my pencil before starting the drawing.

senses.definition: To draw or write with a pencil.
senses.example: We penciled a light grid on the poster first.

senses.definition: An object hung so that it can swing to and fro.
senses.example: The clock’s pendulum swung back and forth.

senses.definition: A kind of bird that cannot fly and uses its flipper-shaped wings to swim.
senses.example: The penguin slid into the water and swam away.

senses.definition: A piece of land with water on most sides and a connection to a larger piece of land.
senses.example: We drove down the peninsula with the ocean to our right and a bay to our left.

senses.definition: In the U.S., a coin worth one cent. In the U.K., one penny is a hundredth of a pound.
senses.example: I found a penny under the bench.

senses.definition: A strongly scented kind of mint, or a candy flavored with it.
senses.example: The peppermint candy made my mouth feel cool.

senses.definition: A way to show an amount out of one hundred.
senses.example: Twenty-five percent of a hundred squares is twenty-five squares.

senses.definition: To sit or balance on a high or narrow spot.
senses.example: The robin perched on a fence post.

senses.definition: A high or narrow place where a bird or another animal can rest.
senses.example: The parakeet hopped onto its perch.

senses.definition: One of several kinds of fish with pointed spines in their fins.
senses.example: A small perch swam near the reeds.

senses.definition: Without a fault or exactly right for the job.
senses.example: That low branch was the perfect place to hang the feeder.

senses.definition: To improve something until it is very good or exactly as you want it.
senses.example: We practiced for a month to perfect the dance.

senses.definition: To do a task or carry out a piece of work.
senses.example: The robot can perform the same movement many times.

senses.definition: To play music, act, dance, or otherwise entertain people who are watching.
senses.example: Our group will perform two songs at the assembly.

senses.definition: A liquid or substance used for its pleasant smell.
senses.example: The perfume smelled faintly like lemons.

senses.definition: To fill a place or thing with a pleasant smell.
senses.example: The blooming flowers perfumed the room.

senses.definition: Maybe or possibly.
senses.example: Perhaps we can fit one more book in the box.

senses.definition: The distance all the way around the edge of a flat shape.
senses.example: Add all four side lengths to find the perimeter of a rectangle.

senses.definition: A stretch of time.
senses.example: We waited a short period before opening the oven.

senses.definition: A small dot used at the end of most complete statements in writing.
senses.example: Put a period after the last word.

senses.definition: A tube with mirrors or similar parts that lets someone see over or around something blocking the view.
senses.example: We used a cardboard periscope to see over the wall.

senses.definition: An extra advantage or benefit.
senses.example: One perk of joining the club was getting to try the new games first.

senses.definition: To make or become more lively or alert, often used with “up.”
senses.example: The dog's ears perked up when we opened the back door.

senses.definition: A layer of ground that stays at or below the freezing point of water for at least two years in a row.
senses.example: Small plants grew only in the soil above the permafrost layer.

senses.definition: A tooth in the set most people keep after losing their first teeth.
senses.example: My first permanent tooth appeared as my jaw grew.

senses.definition: A paved surface with openings that let some water move down through it.
senses.example: Rain sank through the permeable pavement beside the library.

senses.definition: The right to do something or use something that someone else can allow.
senses.example: The app needs permission to use the camera.

senses.definition: To allow something to happen or let someone do it.
senses.example: Our teacher permits talking during the group activity.

senses.definition: A document or record showing that someone has permission to do something.
senses.example: We showed our camping permit at the gate.

senses.definition: To keep trying even when a task is difficult or takes a long time.
senses.example: She persevered until she could play the song without stopping.

senses.definition: To keep trying or continue to happen, even if something makes it difficult.
senses.example: Jules persisted with the puzzle until she found the answer.

senses.definition: A single human being.
senses.example: One person stood near the front of the line to help everyone find a seat.

senses.definition: Details that can help identify a person or tell where to find them.
senses.example: The name of your school can be personal information.

senses.definition: Writing that gives an animal, object, or idea human actions or feelings.
senses.example: “The wind whispered” uses personification.

senses.definition: A way to show depth and how far away things seem on a flat surface.
senses.example: Drawing the road edges closer together gave the picture perspective.

senses.definition: To get someone to believe or do something by giving them reasons.
senses.example: I persuaded my friends to try a shorter route by showing them the map.

senses.definition: An animal, insect, or person that causes damage or repeated annoyance.
senses.example: A garden pest had chewed holes in the leaves.

senses.definition: A part of a flower that is often brightly colored and surrounds the pollen-making or seed-making parts.
senses.example: Five yellow petals surrounded the center of the flower.

senses.definition: A scale used to describe how acidic or basic a water-based liquid is.
senses.example: The colored strip helped us compare the pH of two drinks.

senses.definition: The title for the men and women who ruled ancient Egypt. A ruler with this title is also called a pharaoh.
senses.example: The pharaoh Hatshepsut ordered the building of a large temple.

senses.definition: A trick where someone sends a message that looks real to get private information or get someone to do something unsafe.
senses.example: A grown-up helped us check whether the unexpected sign-in message was phishing.

senses.definition: Plant tissue that carries sugars from where a plant makes or releases them to parts that need them.
senses.example: The leaf sent sugars down the phloem to growing roots.

senses.definition: A device for talking to people far away, often with tools for messages, pictures, and other tasks.
senses.example: I set the alarm on my phone.

senses.definition: To call someone using a phone.
senses.example: I phoned the library to check when it would close.

senses.definition: The upper part of an ocean or lake where enough sunlight can reach for many living things to use it to make food.
senses.example: Plants in the photic zone can catch sunlight under water.

senses.definition: A picture made with a camera.
senses.example: I took a photo of the bird on the railing.

senses.definition: A picture made with a camera.
senses.example: I took a photograph of the round moon over the barn.

senses.definition: To use a camera to take a picture of something.
senses.example: We photographed a new leaf on the plant every day.

senses.definition: A way that plants and some other living things use light energy to make sugars. Most plants use water and carbon dioxide to do this.
senses.example: Leaves use sunlight for photosynthesis.

senses.definition: Growth that bends a plant part toward or away from light.
senses.example: Phototropism turned a seedling’s stem toward the window.

senses.definition: A device that turns energy from light straight into electricity.
senses.example: Many small photovoltaic cells can make up one solar panel.

senses.definition: A small group of words used together as part of a sentence or to express an idea.
senses.example: “In the morning” is a phrase that tells when something happens.

senses.definition: To put something into words in a particular way.
senses.example: Try to phrase your request kindly.

senses.definition: Mostly tiny drifting living things that can make food using sunlight.
senses.example: The phytoplankton used light near the sea surface.

senses.definition: The number you get when you divide the distance around a circle by the distance across its middle. It is about 3.14.
senses.example: We used pi to estimate how far it was around a round table.

senses.definition: A musical instrument with a wide row of keys. In an acoustic piano, pressing a key moves a small hammer that strikes strings inside.
senses.example: Nora played our song on the piano.

senses.definition: A food, often a cucumber, preserved in salty or sour liquid.
senses.example: I put a crunchy pickle next to my sandwich.

senses.definition: A difficult or awkward situation, usually in the phrase “in a pickle.”
senses.example: We were in a pickle when we lost the key to the shed.

senses.definition: To preserve food by keeping it in a liquid such as vinegar or salt water.
senses.example: The shop sold carrots pickled with garlic.

senses.definition: A meal you eat outdoors, often for fun.
senses.example: We spread a blanket beneath the tree for our picnic.

senses.definition: To eat a meal outdoors.
senses.example: Our neighbors picnicked beside the lake.

senses.definition: A graph that uses pictures or symbols to represent numbers.
senses.example: The key on our pictograph says one moon picture stands for five books.

senses.definition: A drawing, painting, or photograph that shows what something looks like.
senses.example: We hung a picture of the ocean in the hall.

senses.definition: To imagine how something looks or happens.
senses.example: I could picture a yellow fence in front of the house.
